Reproducing Iram, Garcia et al. (2024) from dandiset 001350¶

Paper. Iram T, Garcia MA, Amand J, et al. (2024). SRF transcriptionally regulates the oligodendrocyte cytoskeleton during CNS myelination. PNAS 121(12), e2307250121. doi:10.1073/pnas.2307250121. The claims file (claims/001350/10.1073-pnas.2307250121.yaml) was written from the version of record in Europe PMC (PMC10962977) with the SI Appendix; this attempt read the same text and SI Appendix.

Dandiset. DANDI:001350, version 0.250511.1527, "TEM Images of Corpus Callosum in Flox/SRF-cKO Mice". The paper cites no DANDI version (its data statement names only NCBI GEO GSE241561), and this is the only published version, so it is pinned. The draft lists the same 134 assets and the same total size; it is not used.

What the dandiset holds. A BIDS microscopy dataset (no NWB files): 8-bit PNG images of adult corpus callosum at 8000x from 5 SRF-Flox ("WT") and 5 SRF-cKO ("KO") mice, and, under derivatives/labels, masks of myelinated axons with their myelin, unmyelinated axons, oligodendrocyte nuclei and processes for some images. The masks were made for a later segmentation project (AxonDeepSeg pseudo-labels corrected by hand), not by the paper. These are the data of the paper's Figure 2A to 2E and Fig. S3A to S3D. The optic nerve TEM, immunostaining, RNAscope, culture imaging and sequencing data are not in it; the sequencing data are in GEO and are tested in geo_sequencing_claims.ipynb.

Method. The paper scored and measured axons by hand in Fiji. Here the dataset's masks stand in for that scoring (reading O1 of the claims file), and every other reading the claims file names (O2 to O7) is computed. Loading and measures are in srf_tem.py, whose docstring says where each parameter comes from.

The archive summary counts 10 subjects, as the files hold, but 16 samples, where samples.tsv has 86 rows, one per image (the two small regions of sub-373C included), and it lists no species. participants.tsv gives the species as "mus muculus" (a misspelling of Mus musculus). The genotypes are 5 WT and 5 KO, as the description and the paper (n = 5 per genotype) say; the labels WT and KO stand for SRF-Flox and SRF-cKO.

def png_size(url):
    import requests, struct
    head = requests.get(url, headers={"Range": "bytes=0-31"}, timeout=60).content
    w, h = struct.unpack(">II", head[16:24])
    return h, w

with ThreadPoolExecutor(16) as ex:
    shapes = list(ex.map(png_size, assets.set_index("path").loc[imgs.path, "url"]))
imgs["rows"], imgs["cols"] = zip(*shapes)
px = {s: srf_tem.pixel_size_um(s) for s in imgs.subject.unique()}
print("Pixel size by subject (um):", px)
imgs["area_um2"] = imgs.rows * imgs.cols * imgs.subject.map(px) ** 2
imgs["labelled"] = imgs.axonmyelin.notna() & imgs.uaxon.notna()
per_subject = imgs.groupby("subject").agg(
    genotype=("genotype", "first"), images=("path", "size"),
    image_rows=("rows", lambda r: f"{r.min()}-{r.max()}"), image_cols=("cols", lambda c: f"{c.min()}-{c.max()}"),
    imaged_um2=("area_um2", "sum"), labelled_images=("labelled", "sum"),
    labelled_um2=("area_um2", lambda a: a[imgs.loc[a.index, "labelled"]].sum()))
print(per_subject.round(1).to_string())
print("\nMasks by kind:", {k: int(imgs[k].notna().sum()) for k in ["axonmyelin", "uaxon", "nuclei", "process"]})
print("Labelled images by genotype:", imgs[imgs.labelled].groupby("genotype").subject.agg(lambda s: sorted(set(s))).to_dict())

Every subject's sidecar gives the same pixel size, 0.00493 um. Most images are 4675 x 4675 pixels (531 um2 at that scale); sub-366A's sixteen images are smaller (1482 to 2385 rows, 1648 to 2613 columns) and sub-367A to sub-369B's are larger (3412 to 5058 rows, 3712 to 5712 columns). Every mouse has more than 1000 um2 of images, the paper's minimum, so the images could support the paper's design. The masks do not: both kinds of axon mask exist for 8 full images and 2 small regions, from one SRF-Flox mouse (sub-370) and four SRF-cKO mice. The scale cannot be checked against a scale bar, as the images carry none; the measured axon sizes below are consistent with it.

def digest(asset_id):
    return srf_tem.asset_metadata(asset_id)["digest"]["dandi:sha2-256"]

pngs = assets[assets.path.str.endswith(".png")]
with ThreadPoolExecutor(16) as ex:
    digests = dict(zip(pngs.path, ex.map(digest, pngs.asset_id)))
dup = pd.Series(digests).duplicated(keep=False)
print(f"PNG files: {len(digests)}; files sharing a SHA-256 with another: {int(dup.sum())}")

# The two small regions of sub-373C against the README's coordinates (x, y of two corners).
full = srf_tem.read_png("sub-373C/micr/sub-373C_sample-0001_TEM.png")
for chunk, (x0, y0, x1, y1) in {"01": (800, 1500, 1400, 2100), "02": (2400, 1300, 2900, 1800)}.items():
    roi = srf_tem.read_png(f"sub-373C/micr/sub-373C_sample-0001_acq-roi_chunk-{chunk}_TEM.png")
    print(f"chunk-{chunk} {roi.shape}: equal to sample-0001 rows {y0}:{y1}, columns {x0}:{x1}:",
          np.array_equal(full[y0:y1, x0:x1], roi))

# Overlap between labelled images of the same mouse, by phase correlation, with a known overlap as control.
raw = {p: srf_tem.read_png(p) for p in imgs[imgs.labelled & (imgs.rows > 1000)].path}
ctrl = next(iter(raw.values()))
print(f"\ncontrol, two crops of one image overlapping by 3000 x 2000 px: peak {srf_tem.phase_peak(ctrl[:3000, :3000], ctrl[1500:4500, 1000:4000])[0]:.3f}")
rows = []
paths = list(raw)
for i, a in enumerate(paths):
    for b in paths[i + 1:]:
        peak, shift = srf_tem.phase_peak(raw[a], raw[b])
        rows.append({"a": a.split("/")[-1], "b": b.split("/")[-1], "same_mouse": a.split("/")[0] == b.split("/")[0],
                     "peak": round(peak, 4), "shift": shift})
overlap = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(overlap.sort_values("peak", ascending=False).head(8).to_string(index=False))
print("pairs:", len(overlap), "| largest peak:", overlap.peak.max())
del raw

No two files are identical. The two regions of sub-373C are exact crops of its sample-0001 at the README's coordinates, read as (column, row); sample-0001 itself has no masks, so the regions are counted once, as part of sub-373C. No pair of labelled full images shares content: the largest phase-correlation peak between them is printed above, against the control's for a known overlap.

measures = {}
t0 = time.time()
for r in imgs[imgs.labelled].itertuples():
    am, ua = srf_tem.read_png(r.axonmyelin), srf_tem.read_png(r.uaxon)
    assert am.shape == (r.rows, r.cols) == ua.shape
    m = srf_tem.measure_image(am, ua, px[r.subject])
    m["values_axonmyelin"] = sorted(np.unique(am).tolist())
    m["values_uaxon"] = sorted(np.unique(ua).tolist())
    measures[(r.subject, r.sample)] = m
print(f"measured {len(measures)} labelled images in {time.time() - t0:.0f} s")
check = pd.DataFrame([{
    "subject": s, "sample": smp, "genotype": genotype[s], "area_um2": round(m["area_um2"], 1),
    "axonmyelin_values": m["values_axonmyelin"], "uaxon_values": m["values_uaxon"],
    "myelinated": len(m["myelinated"]), "unmyelinated": len(m["unmyelinated"]),
    "axon_specks": m["axon_specks_dropped"], "uaxon_specks": m["uaxon_specks_dropped"],
    "axons_no_myelin": m["axons_without_myelin"], "mask_overlap_px": m["overlap_px"],
    "myelin_unassigned_pct": round(100 * m["myelin_unassigned_px"] / max(m["myelin_px"], 1), 3)}
    for (s, smp), m in measures.items()])
print(check.to_string(index=False))

The axon-and-myelin masks hold axon at 255 (254 in sub-373C chunk-01, which is stored as grey with alpha) and myelin at 127, with a few pixels at 126; the unmyelinated-axon masks are binary. In the two SRF-Flox images no pixel is in both kinds of axon mask; in the cKO images up to 51,098 pixels (0.23% of an image) are. Objects under 20 pixels are dropped as specks (counts above). Myelin not connected to any axon is at most 0.26% of an image's myelin, and every myelinated axon has some myelin assigned.

The masks on their images¶

The masks were made for a segmentation project, so whether they label every axon in an image is not documented. The figure shows a 1000 x 1000 pixel crop (4.93 um a side) from the centre of one SRF-Flox and one SRF-cKO image, the raw image above and the mask outlines below (blue: myelinated axon, orange: outer edge of its myelin, magenta: unmyelinated axon). Grey levels are shown on their full 0 to 255 range; nothing falls outside it. The counts printed are the objects that touch each crop.

In [6]:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import ndimage
from skimage.measure import label as cc_label
from skimage.segmentation import find_boundaries

overlay_images = [("sub-370", "sample-0006"), ("sub-375", "sample-0005")]
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(11, 11))
for j, (s, smp) in enumerate(overlay_images):
    r = imgs[(imgs.subject == s) & (imgs["sample"] == smp)].iloc[0]
    raw = srf_tem.read_png(r.path)
    am, ua = srf_tem.read_png(r.axonmyelin), srf_tem.read_png(r.uaxon)
    r0, c0, w = raw.shape[0] // 2 - 500, raw.shape[1] // 2 - 500, 1000
    sl = (slice(r0, r0 + w), slice(c0, c0 + w))
    axon, myelin = srf_tem.split_axonmyelin(am[sl])
    unmy = ua[sl] > 0
    grey = raw[sl].astype(float) / 255
    rgb = np.repeat(grey[..., None], 3, -1)
    for mask, colour in [((axon | myelin), (0.95, 0.55, 0.1)), (axon, (0.15, 0.45, 0.95)), (unmy, (0.9, 0.1, 0.8))]:
        edge = ndimage.binary_dilation(find_boundaries(cc_label(mask, connectivity=1), mode="inner"))
        rgb[edge] = colour
    axes[0, j].imshow(grey, cmap="gray", vmin=0, vmax=1)
    axes[1, j].imshow(rgb)
    for ax in axes[:, j]:
        ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([])
    axes[0, j].set_title(f"{s} ({genotype[s]}) {smp}, rows {r0}-{r0 + w}, cols {c0}-{c0 + w}")
    n_my = cc_label(axon, connectivity=1).max()
    n_un = cc_label(unmy, connectivity=1).max()
    area = (w * px[s]) ** 2
    print(f"{s} {genotype[s]} {smp}: crop {area:.1f} um2, grey {raw[sl].min()} to {raw[sl].max()}; "
          f"myelinated axons {n_my} ({n_my / area:.2f} per um2), unmyelinated axon objects {n_un} "
          f"({n_un / area:.2f} per um2)")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

sub-370 WT sample-0006: crop 24.3 um2, grey 0 to 236; myelinated axons 40 (1.65 per um2), unmyelinated axon objects 63 (2.59 per um2)

sub-375 KO sample-0005: crop 24.3 um2, grey 0 to 255; myelinated axons 17 (0.70 per um2), unmyelinated axon objects 249 (10.24 per um2)

In both crops every myelinated fibre visible in the image has an axon and a myelin outline, and nearly every small unmyelinated profile has an outline; the masks do not look incomplete. This is a check by eye on two crops of 24 um2, not a measure of completeness over the 4264 um2 the masks cover. The SRF-cKO crop includes part of a cell body (lower right), which holds no axons.

With the stated pixel size, myelinated axons in adult corpus callosum measure a few hundred nanometres to about a micrometre, myelin about 100 nm, and unmyelinated axons about 0.2 um, sizes consistent with adult mouse corpus callosum; this is consistent with the stated scale, not a proof of it. The images have no time base, so the protocol's check of a shared clock does not apply.

How the claims are tested¶

The claims file's criteria call for per-mouse values from 5 SRF-Flox and 5 SRF-cKO mice and an unpaired two-tailed t test (Methods, "Data Analysis and Statistics": "Statistical significance was determined between biological replicate ... by an unpaired, two-tailed t test"; Figure 2C to 2E legends, "n = 5 animals from each genotype"). The paper's per-axon scoring is not deposited, and the masks that stand in for it (reading O1) cover one SRF-Flox mouse (sub-370) and four SRF-cKO mice. The per-mouse measurements the test needs are missing for four of the five SRF-Flox mice and one of the five SRF-cKO mice, so each claim below is blocked as data_missing. A t test with one Flox mouse has no estimate of the Flox spread: Student's test borrows the cKO variance, and Welch's test is undefined. Each section still shows every value the masks allow, under every reading the claims file names: the per-mouse values, the group means against the expected values, the Student t test of the one Flox mouse against the cKO mice (not the paper's design), and, as a variant, tests over images (which treat images as independent, unlike the paper).

The dandiset's description points to a segmentation model trained on these masks (github.com/axondeepseg/model_seg_unmyelinated_tem), which could label the other 76 full images. It is not used. The paper does not rely on it (the claims file says it is not the paper's code), so under the protocol it cannot be brought in as an outside input; it was trained on the very images labelled here, and its uncorrected output on the other mice would be a further step from the paper's hand scoring than the hand-corrected masks are. It is an nnU-Net model meant for a GPU; this runner has 4 CPUs and none.

sub-373C has only two small regions (15 um2), far below the paper's minimum area; it is shown, and each result is also given without it.

In [8]:
def student_one_vs_many(x_cko, x_flox):
    "Student's pooled t test, which is defined when one group has a single value; Welch's is not."
    a, b = np.asarray(x_cko, float), np.asarray(x_flox, float)
    na, nb = len(a), len(b)
    ss = ((a - a.mean()) ** 2).sum() + ((b - b.mean()) ** 2).sum()
    df = na + nb - 2
    sp = np.sqrt(ss / df)
    t = (a.mean() - b.mean()) / (sp * np.sqrt(1 / na + 1 / nb))
    return t, df, 2 * stats.t.sf(abs(t), df)

def welch(x_cko, x_flox):
    if min(len(x_cko), len(x_flox)) < 2:
        return np.nan, np.nan
    r = stats.ttest_ind(x_cko, x_flox, equal_var=False)
    return r.statistic, r.pvalue

def group_table(values, name, expected_flox, expected_cko):
    "values: per-mouse Series indexed by subject. Group means, tests, with and without sub-373C."
    rows = []
    for label, keep in [("all labelled mice", values.index), ("without sub-373C", values.index.drop("sub-373C", errors="ignore"))]:
        v = values.loc[keep]
        flox = v[[genotype[s] == "WT" for s in v.index]]
        cko = v[[genotype[s] == "KO" for s in v.index]]
        t, df, p = student_one_vs_many(cko, flox)
        wt, wp = welch(cko, flox)
        rows.append({"mice": label, "n_flox": len(flox), "n_cko": len(cko),
                     "flox_mean": flox.mean(), "cko_mean": cko.mean(), "cko_minus_flox": cko.mean() - flox.mean(),
                     "cko_over_flox": cko.mean() / flox.mean(),
                     "flox_in_tol": abs(flox.mean() - expected_flox[0]) <= expected_flox[1],
                     "cko_in_tol": abs(cko.mean() - expected_cko[0]) <= expected_cko[1],
                     "student_t": t, "df": df, "student_p": p, "welch_p": wp})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("mice")

def image_test(per_image, col):
    "Variant, not the paper's design: images as units."
    f = per_image[per_image.genotype == "WT"][col]
    c = per_image[per_image.genotype == "KO"][col]
    return {"n_images_flox": len(f), "n_images_cko": len(c), "flox_mean": f.mean(), "cko_mean": c.mean(),
            "student_p": stats.ttest_ind(c, f).pvalue, "welch_p": stats.ttest_ind(c, f, equal_var=False).pvalue}

fig2c-cc-percent-myelinated¶

In the adult corpus callosum SRF-cKO mice have a lower percentage of myelinated axons than SRF-Flox littermates (about 22% against about 37%, read from the figure), so the hypomyelination seen in optic nerve persists into adulthood in corpus callosum.

Expected: SRF-Flox 37 +/- 3.7%, SRF-cKO 22 +/- 2.2%; unpaired t test p < 0.05 under readings O1, O2, O4 and O7; axons counted per mouse reported against the paper's minimum of 2,500.

Result: blocked (data missing: masks for one SRF-Flox mouse). The claim's per-mouse test of 5 against 5 mice cannot be run. That mouse, sub-370, has 26.3% of its axons myelinated (readings O2a and O4a; 26.3% to 28.2% over the four readings), below the expected 37 +/- 3.7%. The four cKO mice average 14.3% (14.3% to 18.9%), below the expected 22 +/- 2.2%, and lower than the Flox mouse under every reading, with Student p 0.13 to 0.20 for one Flox mouse against the cKO mice. With images as units, Student p is 0.014 (O4a) and 0.036 (O4b), Welch p 0.12 and 0.19. sub-370 has 3,842 axons counted, above the paper's 2,500. Counting unmyelinated axons without the pixels that are also in a myelinated fibre changes no mouse's percent by more than 0.02 points. The direction of the paper's effect is present in these masks; both genotypes are below the paper's values.

Result: blocked (data missing: masks for one SRF-Flox mouse). sub-370 has 0.95 myelinated axons per um2 (1.04 with edge axons kept), against the expected 1.8 +/- 0.18 under the claims file's unit; the cKO means are 0.78 to 1.13, against 1.42 +/- 0.142. Every mouse with whole labelled images has 0.82 to 1.09 myelinated axons per um2: 0.53 of the paper's value in the Flox mouse and 0.58 to 0.69 of it in the cKO mice (up to 0.77 with edge axons kept), so the masks and the paper's counts differ before any question of the number of mice. The masks hold 3.62 axons per um2 in all in sub-370, 26% below the 4.86 that the paper's Fig. 2C and 2D together imply, and 4.8 to 6.9 in the cKO mice with whole images, against 6.5. In the Flox mouse both factors are low: all axons per um2 at 0.74 of the paper's and the fraction myelinated at 0.71 of it (26% against 37%), and together they give the 0.53. The crops above show no obvious gaps in the masks. What remains open is the image scale (no scale bar to check it), the unit of Fig. 2D, and which regions the paper scored. The cKO to Flox ratio is 0.81 with edge axons left out and all four cKO mice (inside 0.79 +/- 0.079), 0.97 without sub-373C, and 1.08 or 0.97 with edge axons kept. No reading gives a Student p below 0.63. The one-Flox-mouse density test over images raises a scipy precision warning, as sub-370's two images have nearly equal densities; that variant's p is not reliable.

def morph_tables(seed_offset=0):
    out = {}
    for diameter in ["eq", "feret"]:
        for keep_edge in [False, True]:
            for sample in [False, True]:
                rng = np.random.default_rng(srf_tem.RANDOM_SEED + seed_offset)
                key = f"O5{'a' if diameter == 'eq' else 'b'} O4{'b' if keep_edge else 'a'} O6{'b' if sample else 'a'}"
                out[key] = srf_tem.mouse_morphometry(axons, diameter, keep_edge, sample, rng)
    return out

morph = morph_tables()
print("Per mouse values under O5a (equivalent circle), O4a (edges left out), O6a (all axons):")
print(morph["O5a O4a O6a"].assign(genotype=[genotype[s] for s in morph["O5a O4a O6a"].index]).round(4).to_string())

def morph_section(col, expected_flox, expected_cko, claim_rng_offset):
    res = {k: group_table(v[col].astype(float), col, expected_flox, expected_cko) for k, v in morph.items()}
    show = pd.concat({k: v for k, v in res.items()}, names=["reading"])
    print(show[["n_flox", "n_cko", "flox_mean", "cko_mean", "cko_minus_flox", "flox_in_tol", "cko_in_tol",
                "student_p", "welch_p"]].round(4).to_string())
    print(f"\n{len(show)} combinations of reading and subset: Flox in tolerance {int(show.flox_in_tol.sum())}, "
          f"cKO in tolerance {int(show.cko_in_tol.sum())}, cKO above Flox {int((show.cko_minus_flox > 0).sum())}; "
          f"Flox mean {show.flox_mean.min():.4g} to {show.flox_mean.max():.4g}, cKO mean {show.cko_mean.min():.4g} to "
          f"{show.cko_mean.max():.4g}, cKO minus Flox {show.cko_minus_flox.min():.4g} to {show.cko_minus_flox.max():.4g}, "
          f"Student p {show.student_p.min():.3g} to {show.student_p.max():.3g}")
    # Spread of the O6b result over 100 draws (O5a, O4a), with a generator of this claim's own.
    rng = np.random.default_rng(srf_tem.RANDOM_SEED + claim_rng_offset)
    draws = []
    for _ in range(100):
        v = srf_tem.mouse_morphometry(axons, "eq", False, True, rng)[col].astype(float)
        f = v[[genotype[s] == "WT" for s in v.index]].mean()
        c = v[[genotype[s] == "KO" for s in v.index]].mean()
        draws.append((f, c, student_one_vs_many(v[[genotype[s] == "KO" for s in v.index]], v[[genotype[s] == "WT" for s in v.index]])[2]))
    d = np.array(draws)
    print(f"\nO6b over 100 draws (O5a, O4a): Flox mean {d[:,0].min():.4f} to {d[:,0].max():.4f}; "
          f"cKO mean {d[:,1].min():.4f} to {d[:,1].max():.4f}; Student p {d[:,2].min():.3g} to {d[:,2].max():.3g}")
    return res

The cKO mean is 0.675 to 0.710, below the Flox value under every reading (cKO minus Flox -0.009 to -0.026, where the paper reports +0.057), with Student p 0.29 to 0.77. Over 100 random draws of 100 axons the Flox mean spans 0.702 to 0.733. With images as units the Flox mean is 0.721 and the cKO mean 0.700 (Welch p 0.077). In these masks the difference runs the other way from the paper's in every combination; with one Flox mouse this cannot be told apart from the spread between mice.

A claim of absence is judged on the paper's test, a Student t test on 5 against 5 per-mouse means, which cannot be run with one labelled SRF-Flox mouse. The Flox mouse's mean myelin thickness is 96.5 to 110.0 nm over the readings (inside 105 +/- 10.5); the cKO mean is 97.4 to 112.5 nm (cKO minus Flox -3.4 to +11.6 nm), mostly above the expected 93 +/- 9.3. The Student test of one mouse against the cKO mice gives p 0.085 to 0.99, and over images p 0.21 (Welch 0.24).

Result: blocked (data missing: masks for one SRF-Flox mouse). Its mean myelinated axon diameter is 478 to 618 nm over the readings (inside 530 +/- 53 in 10 of 16 reading and subset combinations), and the cKO mean is 446 to 569 nm, smaller than the Flox value in 15 of the 16 combinations, against the expected 625 +/- 62.5. The one Student p below 0.05 (0.010, O5b, O4a, O6b, without sub-373C) has cKO smaller than Flox, the reverse of the claim. With images as units, Flox 595 nm and cKO 549 nm (Welch p 0.085). As for the g-ratio, the masks show the reverse of the paper's direction, which one Flox mouse cannot separate from the spread between mice.

Summary¶

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

Claim Data Outcome

GSEA and single-nucleus RNA-seq (4 claims) elsewhere (GEO GSE241561) blocked: not runnable

How the analysis differs from the paper's. The paper scored axons by hand in Fiji over at least 1000 um2 and 2,500 axons per mouse, for 5 mice per genotype. Here the dataset's masks, made later for a segmentation project, stand in for that scoring; they cover 8 full images and two small regions, from one SRF-Flox and four SRF-cKO mice. Diameters come from object areas or minimum Feret widths, not a line drawn by hand.

In the masks, percent myelinated is lower in every cKO mouse than in the one Flox mouse, as in the paper, but both genotypes are below the paper's values; myelinated axons per um2 are 0.53 of the paper's value in the Flox mouse and 0.58 to 0.69 of it in the cKO mice; and the g-ratio and myelinated axon diameter differences run the other way from the paper's. None of this decides an outcome, as one Flox mouse cannot be compared with five.

What was found about the dataset. The raw images of all 10 mice are there, more than 1000 um2 per mouse, but no per-axon measurement of the paper is deposited, and the masks cover one of the five SRF-Flox mice. The archive summary counts 16 samples where samples.tsv lists 86 and no species; participants.tsv misspells the species ("mus muculus"). Only the corpus callosum TEM of the paper is in the dandiset; the sequencing data are in GEO.
